about: Canonical ground truth for what the operator can see and do, independent of any one surface. Both the daemon's web dashboard and the desktop app are checked against it by tools/operator_surfaces_spec_test.py. Change THIS first, in the same PR as the route or the screen. See README.md.

places.me: who am I and what is mine
places.activity: what happened, and what needs me

rules.text: Any act that PERMITS (approve, grant, ratify, register, delegate) carries a stated reason, recorded on the chain; refusing does not require one. The asymmetry is preserved, never inverted. Surfaces refuse an empty reason before the daemon sees it.
A single-shot decision answered 409 renders as 'already decided elsewhere' and re-reads; it is not shown as a failure.
A write whose meaning depends on state the operator reviewed sends that state, and the daemon refuses (409) if it moved. The surface shows what moved.
An unmeasurable answer (UNKNOWN) is never rendered as fine, never as an empty list, and never silently replaced by the last known state.
Members are identified by MEMBER id (e.g. kimi-code), never by atlas id (kimi_code_cli) or plugin directory (kimi).
An act that destroys or replaces something unrecoverable asks for explicit confirmation (typed name for deletes).
Vault values are never displayed or re-fetched; lists carry names and policy only.
Operator writes are ABSENT, not disabled-looking, without an operator session.

A write that defines what is trusted names the items it applies to, and changes only those. A bulk form is accepted only when every item matches the independent record (for gates: the deploy record); otherwise it is refused and the non-matching items are named. The surface shows each item's status against that record beside its control.
rules.source: dp, 2026-09-28: "currently gate ratify button ratifies all - including mismatched and non-deployed. it should either only ratify gates that match deployment, or provide a by-gate ratification"

capabilities.title: Rule on a pending gate escalation
obligations: each pending escalation shows the daemon-MEASURED write effect of its retained act (evidence::write_effect), never the member's description of it; an act the daemon cannot measure shows no effect rather than a guessed one

a copy-shaped act (cp <source> <governed>) shows the source's line count and the sha256 the approval binds, and a +/- line diff against the copy currently ENFORCING, labelled as that (not as the act's destination); a no-op is said, not left to two zeros

a patch-application act (git apply|am <patch>, patch -i|<) shows the patch's sha256 the approval binds, the number of files, each target path with +/- counts and created/deleted, and the patch text; a patch the daemon cannot read is shown as unreadable, and a patch above the measurement cap says the approval does not bind its bytes
any rendered diff or patch text that was cut says so ("TRUNCATED"), so the reader never concludes they have seen the whole change

a patch's per-file summary represents mode changes, renames, copies and binary files (a file section with no ---/+++ pair is still a file), and when the summary does not represent the whole patch (summary_complete=false) the surface says INCOMPLETE and names what is missing; a patch or copy source above the measurement cap is NOT read, and the surface says so instead of showing counts

capabilities.title: Rule on a scope request
obligations: a request the GATE opened on a refused act (origin gate_deny) is shown as that: the rule (mrh.path / mrh.command), the tool, and the refused act verbatim, labelled as the act the operator is ruling on and never as the member's reason; how many times the member re-issued it is shown beside it

the operator chooses the DURATION at decide time, from exactly these: this act once (once:true; offered only when once_available, i.e. the gate recorded an act to bind), for the session (memory-only, expires), or standing (vault, survives restart); refusing is a separate control that needs no reason

the operator chooses the BREADTH at decide time for session and standing grants: the exact asked path (the default), or a directory above it, which is always recursive (grant_path + recursive:true); every offered directory is an ancestor of the asked path at a separator and never the root, and the control shows the path the grant will reach before it is sent
a request whose refused reach was a glob over a directory (subtree:true) says that only a recursive grant covers it, and the surface does not offer an exact session or standing grant for it
a one-time approval says that it is spent by the identical act, once, inside the claim window, and is never served as standing policy

PEER ROUTING (dp, 2026-10-05: "scope escalations should go to peers not to me"): a gate-opened request from a proven asker is decided by a NOT-SAME peer (hestia_scope_peer_decide / hestia scope decide --as). The surface shows the invited peers and labels the queue as awaiting a peer, read-only; the decide controls are labelled as the OPERATOR OVERRIDE, never as the default route, and the queue is not announced as awaiting the operator. A request no peer can clear (asserted asker, or no admissible peer) is labelled as the operator's
a ruling made by a peer is shown read-only with the deciding peer (granted_by peer:<id>) and its NOT-SAME basis (independence, asker basis); the operator can revoke it (scope-revoke) like any grant
capabilities.notes: Reconciled 2026-10-05 (scope refusal -> escalation with a standing option): both surfaces send duration (once / session / standing) and breadth (grant_path, recursive) in the one decide call. Peer routing 2026-10-05: the operator's decide is the override; peers decide through the MCP door, not this route.

capabilities.title: Bypass / restore a member's gate: a fail-OPEN recovery switch for a member its own gate has locked out
obligations: offered per member whose harness registers a hestia gate, keyed by MEMBER id (the daemon derives the gate and its registration from the inventory, never from the surface)

bypass carries a stated reason; the confirm says the member then acts UNGOVERNED (no gate, no scope, no safety preset, no escalations) until restored, that a running harness may keep its old hook until it restarts, and that the act is recorded on the chain
while a bypass is active (GET /api/agents `bypassed`) the member shows a persistent BYPASSED badge with when and why, and its control is Restore
a restore the daemon refuses (the registration changed since the bypass) is shown with the daemon's reason and is not retried

no surface labels a bypassed member miswired on its own: the inventory's verdict is shown unchanged (dp: a bypassed harness should be flagged miswired by the existing detection, and this is the test of it)
capabilities.notes: dp, 2026-09-28: "this is useful for instances when an update locks out a member that we need to be active to fix the issues. happens frequently still". Restore is the refusing direction and needs no reason.

capabilities.title: Gate integrity: installed vs ratified vs deployed
obligations: each gate row shows its deployment status: match | differs | not-deployed | no-deploy-record | unreadable
a ratified expectation whose path is no longer a discovered gate is shown as stale (discovered: false)
whether ratify-all would be accepted (bulk_ratify.allowed) is shown, with the gates that block it
each row carries forgettable and, when not, forget_blocked_reason; not_registered: true marks a ratified gate whose member still declares a gate but no gate is registered

capabilities.title: Ratify gates as the trusted build: per gate, or all at once only when every gate is the deployed bytes
obligations: every discovered gate row carries its own ratify control, which sends paths: [that gate] and expected for exactly that gate
a per-gate ratify changes only that gate's expectation; every other gate's ratification is untouched
ratify-all sends no paths and is offered only when bulk_ratify.allowed; the daemon refuses it (409, naming the gates) otherwise
a surface must not offer per-gate controls to a daemon whose verify has no bulk_ratify (it predates per-gate and would ratify every gate)

capabilities.title: Forget a stale gate expectation (a path no gate is wired at any more)
obligations: offered only on rows the daemon marks forgettable: true in GET /api/gates/verify, one path per control; the surface renders the daemon's judgement, never its own
the daemon refuses to forget a gate it still discovers: that would turn a MODIFIED finding into a merely unratified one

the daemon refuses to forget an expectation whose member is installed, not retired, and still declares a gate role: a ratified gate that is no longer registered is a bypass or a miswire, not a stale row (hestia #1156). Forget becomes available once the member is retired or uninstalled

a row that is not discovered while its member still declares a gate is shown with a prominent NOT REGISTERED — possible bypass badge and the daemon's forget_blocked_reason, instead of a forget control
